name: ecs:ExecuteCommand + ecs:DescribeTasks
description: Execute a command in a running ECS task via ECS Exec to retrieve the task role's temporary credentials from the container metadata endpoint
author: Seth Art

required.description: Must have permission on ECS tasks in clusters with ECS Exec enabled
Required by the AWS CLI to retrieve the container runtime ID for establishing the SSM session

additional.description: Helpful for discovering ECS clusters in the account
Helpful for discovering task ARNs in the target cluster
Useful for viewing the task definition to discover the task role ARN

admin: An ECS service must have ECS Exec explicitly enabled (enable_execute_command = true)
The service must have at least one running task with an administrative task role
The ECS Exec agent (SSM agent) must be running and healthy in the container
The AWS Systems Manager Session Manager plugin must be installed locally
lateral: An ECS service must have ECS Exec explicitly enabled (enable_execute_command = true)
The service must have at least one running task with a privileged task role
The ECS Exec agent (SSM agent) must be running and healthy in the container
The AWS Systems Manager Session Manager plugin must be installed locally

references.title: AWS - Using Amazon ECS Exec to access containers

techniques: T1552.005 - Unsecured Credentials: Cloud Instance Metadata API

options.name: CLUSTER_NAME
options.description: ECS cluster name or ARN containing the target task

options.name: TASK_ARN
options.description: Target ECS task ARN to execute command on (auto-discovered if not set)

options.name: CONTAINER_NAME
options.description: Container name within the task (auto-detected from task definition if not set)
